summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and gout was admitted with acute shortness of breath and chest pain. He had developed worsening dyspnea after his last dialysis session, associated with a recent upper respiratory infection. Imaging and labs revealed pulmonary edema and severe fluid overload, with a BNP over 70,000 and admission troponin elevation to 0.17, peaking at 0.38 without MB fraction rise or EKG changes. He was treated with nitroglycerin infusion and emergent hemodialysis, removing 3.2 liters initially and 2.4 liters on the second day. His symptoms improved, and he was weaned from BiPAP. The chest pain was atypical and not indicative of acute coronary syndrome. He was discharged home with instructions to continue dialysis, start benzonatate for cough, and adjust cinacalcet dose, with home health follow-up.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Chronic total occlusion of coronary artery
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
